decision_reason: A1 is broadly useful but leaves the low-U_NN lying-pair indistinguishable in posture inclination, does not explicitly encode ascending-versus-descending direction, and conflates elevator displacement with self-generated locomotion. The highest-D_kNN unseen classes also need more transferable distinctions from standing and treadmill or cross-trainer anchors. The refinement adds only IMU-observable posture direction, vertical directionality, lateral posture orientation, and whole-body coupling.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular or rotational motion during the activity.

attributes.name: locomotor_translation
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained self-generated body progression through space, distinguished from displacement or acceleration caused primarily by an elevator.

levels.Low: Little or no self-generated locomotor progression.

attributes.name: motion_regularity
attributes.definition: Temporal consistency and predictability of the motion pattern.

levels.Low: Irregular and poorly predictable motion pattern.
levels.Medium: Partly structured motion with moderate variability.

attributes.name: lateral_posture
attributes.definition: Degree to which the global load-bearing body configuration is oriented toward a lateral side rather than upright or back-oriented.

levels.Medium: Oblique configuration between back-oriented and side-oriented.

attributes.name: vertical_directionality
attributes.definition: Dominant direction of sustained vertical progression or load-related motion relative to gravity.

attributes.name: whole_body_coupling
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion of the torso, arms, and legs is coordinated within a common activity pattern.

levels.Low: Motion is localized or weakly coordinated across body regions.
levels.Medium: Several body regions participate with partial coordination.
levels.High: Torso, upper limbs, and lower limbs show strongly coordinated motion.

operations.reason: motion_intensity remains a physically distinct coarse separator for static, locomotor, and vigorous activities. Supporting groups: G3 and G4. Expected sensor evidence is overall acceleration and angular-motion magnitude with temporal intensity variation across torso and limbs. Prediction ambiguity remains because activities with different mechanics can have similar overall energy; it is therefore retained as a transferable anchor rather than used alone.
seen_anchors: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)
running on a treadmill with a speed of 8 km/h

operations.reason: cadence provides a stable periodic-rate contrast among stairs, treadmill locomotion, cycling, and irregular elevator movement. Supporting group: G6. Expected sensor evidence is repetition rate and periodicity in accelerometer and gyroscope signals from limbs and torso. Prediction ambiguity occurs when activities share similar repetition rates, so cadence is preserved alongside motion quality and direction attributes.
seen_anchors: cycling on an exercise bike in horizontal positions
walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)

operations.reason: smoothness remains useful for separating controlled cyclic exercise from impact-rich stairs, jumping, and basketball. Supporting groups: G9 and G8. Expected sensor evidence is sustained rapid signal change and spectral dispersion across body-mounted inertial signals. Prediction ambiguity is possible for transitions within an activity, but the concept is physically observable and complementary to impulsiveness.
seen_anchors: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)

operations.reason: impulsiveness directly captures impact-like peaks that distinguish descending stairs and jumping from smooth exercise. Supporting group: G10. Expected sensor evidence is peak jerk in torso and leg accelerometers and corresponding gyroscope changes. Prediction ambiguity arises when impacts are weak or intermittent, but the attribute remains independently supported and transferable from jumping and stair anchors.

posture_inclination remains a direct gravity-relative distinction among upright, inclined, and near-horizontal configurations. Supporting group: G1. Expected sensor evidence is static gravity orientation, especially from the torso sensor. Prediction ambiguity is substantial between different horizontal postures, which motivates the separate lateral_posture attribute rather than changing this physically valid concept.
seen_anchors: cycling on an exercise bike in horizontal positions

operations.reason: posture_variability supplies a distinct temporal contrast for rowing, basketball, and moving around in an elevator. Supporting group: G12 and G5. Expected sensor evidence is gravity-angle change and gradual posture transitions at the torso. Prediction ambiguity exists when only local limbs move, but the global-load-bearing definition limits that ambiguity.

rotational_motion remains a useful mechanical contrast for cycling, cross-trainer exercise, rowing, and irregular locomotion. Supporting group: G2. Expected sensor evidence is sustained angular motion from gyroscopes across torso and limbs. Prediction ambiguity occurs because arm and leg rotation can produce similar aggregate levels; it is retained as a broad transferable attribute.
seen_anchors: cycling on an exercise bike in vertical positions

operations.reason: locomotor_translation refines the original translation concept by distinguishing self-generated progression from apparent displacement or acceleration due to an elevator. Supporting groups: G13, G14, and G3. Expected sensor evidence is short-window velocity proxies combined with coordinated multiaxial torso and leg motion. Prediction ambiguity is expected because an IMU may not perfectly separate elevator-induced motion from body locomotion; the concept is nevertheless more physically targeted for the elevator versus walking contrast.
seen_anchors: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)

operations.reason: motion_regularity remains complementary to cadence because it captures predictability rather than repetition rate alone. Supporting groups: G11 and G6. Expected sensor evidence is recurrence, temporal consistency, and periodic structure across inertial channels. Prediction ambiguity occurs for short windows or mixed movements, but the attribute is supported by seen treadmill, cycling, and irregular basketball anchors.
seen_anchors: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in flat)

operations.reason: lateral_posture adds the missing observable distinction between lying on back and lying on right side, which A1 posture_inclination cannot provide because both are near-horizontal. Supporting group: G1, with G14 for axis interpretation. Expected sensor evidence is the static gravity vector and torso orientation relative to the body axis. Prediction ambiguity can arise from sensor mounting variation or partially rotated postures, so the levels intentionally represent broad orientation bands rather than fine side-specific angles.

vertical_directionality adds a direct ascending-versus-descending contrast that is absent from A1 and is especially important for the low-U_NN stair pair. Supporting groups: G1, G5, G13, and G14. Expected sensor evidence is gravity-referenced acceleration, temporal trend, and coordinated torso-leg motion during upward or downward progression. Prediction ambiguity is expected during level segments, reversals, or brief windows; the attribute therefore uses broad dominant-direction levels and complements, rather than replaces, intensity and impulsiveness.
seen_anchors: walking on a treadmill with a speed of 4 km/h (in 15 deg inclined positions)

operations.reason: whole_body_coupling supplies a physically meaningful distinction for rowing and other high-D_kNN activities by describing coordinated torso, arm, and leg participation rather than merely total intensity or rotation. Supporting groups: G14, G2, and G12. Expected sensor evidence is cross-body multiaxial acceleration-rotation coupling and synchronized posture changes across the torso and limb sensors. Prediction ambiguity is possible because cross-trainer exercise and basketball also involve multiple body regions; broad coordination levels are preferred over a fine-grained rowing-specific pattern.
seen_anchors: cycling on an exercise bike in horizontal positions

semantic_redundancy_review: motion_intensity, impulsiveness, and smoothness are related but distinct: magnitude, peak abruptness, and continuity respectively. cadence and motion_regularity separate repetition rate from temporal predictability. posture_inclination and lateral_posture separate gravity-relative tilt magnitude from orientation toward a side, while posture_variability captures change over time. locomotor_translation narrows translational_motion to self-generated progression and is intentionally distinct from whole_body_coupling, which describes cross-body coordination. vertical_directionality adds signed progression direction rather than another intensity dimension. The final set contains no deliberately duplicated attribute.
